text.p: Amalgamated Holdings Ltd said it has set targets for continued earnings growth through a significant expansion of its cinema and hotel operations and new business plans for Australia and overseas.

"We have set targets for continued earnings growth through a significant expansion of our cinema and hotel divisions and new businsess opportunities both in Australia and overseas," chairman Allan Rydge said in a statement.
Earlier, Amalagamated reported a 6.5 percent fall in net profit to A$38.04 million for the year to June 30, 1996.

Rydge said the group's Greater Union division will open three new cinema centres before Christmas. The hotel business, Rydges Hotels and Resorts has already announced two new properties due to open in the next 12 months.

He said box office revenues in Greater Union and Birch Carroll and Coyle should strengthen further in 1996/97 with a continuing supply of strong film product and the addition of new screens to both circuits.
"The outlook for Rydges and Resorts remains very positive with further improvements in yield and occupancy and the addition of new management agreements," Rydge said.
"Kosciusko Thredbo has enjoyed good snow conditions in recent weeks and this should ensure a strong result for the 1996 winter season," Rydge said.
"Property and development sales (at Kosciusko Thredbo) are expected to make a strong contribution to profit in 1996/97," he said.

He said the company is continuing to pursue a numbe rof opportunities for expansion of its business mix. These discussions follow the decision earlier this year not to further pursue the acquisition of cruise operator Blue Line Cruises.
At 11.55 a.m. (0155 GMT), Amalgamated shares were A$1.00 or 3.51 percent up to A$29.50, a record high.
